claims.quote: The central, coordinating process which stores configuration, loads plugins, and renders the various user interfaces for Jenkins.

claims.claim: A label is text that groups agents by capability.

claims.claim: The agent section says where the pipeline or a stage runs.
claims.quote: The `agent` section specifies where the entire Pipeline, or a specific stage, will execute in the Jenkins environment depending on where the `agent` section is placed.

claims.claim: agent { label } runs on an agent with that label.
claims.quote: Execute the Pipeline, or stage, on an agent available in the Jenkins environment with the provided label.

claims.claim: A label can be an expression such as 'a && b'.
claims.quote: agent { label 'my-label1 && my-label2' }

claims.claim: agent none at the top forces each stage to name its own agent.

claims.claim: A Jenkinsfile in source control gives the pipeline code review and an audit trail.
claims.quote: Code review/iteration on the Pipeline

claims.claim: The parameters directive lists values a user gives when starting a run.
claims.quote: The `parameters` directive provides a list of parameters that a user should provide when triggering the Pipeline.

claims.claim: The when directive decides whether a stage runs.
claims.quote: The `when` directive allows the Pipeline to determine whether the stage should be executed depending on the given condition.

claims.claim: With beforeAgent true, when is evaluated before an agent is taken.
claims.quote: If `beforeAgent` is set to `true`, the `when` condition will be evaluated first, and the `agent` will only be entered if the `when` condition evaluates to true.

claims.claim: A stage may hold parallel stages.
claims.quote: Stages in Declarative Pipeline may have a `parallel` section containing a list of nested stages to be run in parallel.

claims.claim: A stage inside parallel can have its own agent, when and nested sequential stages, but no parallel of its own.
claims.quote: However, a `stage` directive within a `parallel` or `matrix` block can use all other functionality of a `stage`, including `agent`, `tools`, `when`, etc.

claims.claim: A stage has exactly one of steps, stages, parallel or matrix.
claims.quote: A stage must have one and only one of `steps`, `stages`, `parallel`, or `matrix`.

claims.claim: Post conditions run in the documented order: always, changed, fixed, regression, aborted, failure, success, unstable, unsuccessful, cleanup.
claims.quote: The condition blocks are executed in the order shown below.

claims.claim: always runs whatever the result.
claims.quote: Run the steps in the `post` section regardless of the completion status of the Pipeline's or stage's run.

claims.claim: changed runs when the result differs from the previous run's.
claims.quote: Only run the steps in `post` if the current Pipeline's run has a different completion status from its previous run.

claims.claim: fixed runs when a run succeeds after a failed or unstable one.
claims.quote: Only run the steps in `post` if the current Pipeline's run is successful and the previous run failed or was unstable.

claims.claim: aborted runs for an aborted run, usually a manual abort.
claims.quote: Only run the steps in `post` if the current Pipeline's run has an "aborted" status, usually due to the Pipeline being manually aborted.

claims.claim: failure runs for a failed status.
claims.quote: Only run the steps in `post` if the current Pipeline's or stage's run has a "failed" status

claims.claim: success runs for a success status.
claims.quote: Only run the steps in `post` if the current Pipeline's or stage's run has a "success" status

claims.claim: unsuccessful runs for any status but success.
claims.quote: Only run the steps in `post` if the current Pipeline's or stage's run has not a "success" status.

claims.claim: cleanup runs after every other post condition, whatever the result.
claims.quote: Run the steps in this `post` condition after every other `post` condition has been evaluated, regardless of the Pipeline or stage's status.

claims.claim: stash saves files for use on any node in the same run.
claims.quote: Saves a set of files for later use on any node/workspace in the same Pipeline run.

claims.claim: Stashes are discarded when the run ends, unless preserveStashes keeps them for restarts.
claims.quote: By default, stashed files are discarded at the end of a pipeline run.

claims.claim: A stash is not available to other runs, pipelines or jobs; archiveArtifacts is for that.
claims.quote: Stashes from one Pipeline run are not available in other runs, other Pipelines, or other jobs. If you want to persist artifacts for use outside of a single run, consider using archiveArtifacts instead.

claims.claim: stash and unstash are designed for small files.
claims.quote: Note that the stash and unstash steps are designed for use with small files.

claims.claim: There is no hard limit; from somewhere between 5 and 100 MB, alternatives are advised.
claims.quote: There's not a hard stash size limit, but between 5-100 MB you should probably consider alternatives.

claims.claim: The controller compresses each stash, which costs it CPU for large files.
claims.quote: This is because stashed files are archived in a compressed TAR, and with large files this demands considerable resources on the controller, particularly CPU time.

claims.claim: For large transfers the step's help points to an external repository manager.
claims.quote: For large data transfers, use the External Workspace Manager plugin, or use an external repository manager such as Nexus or Artifactory.

claims.claim: unstash retrieves a stash from the controller into the current workspace.
claims.quote: `unstash` will retrieve the named "stash" from the Jenkins controller into the Pipeline's current workspace.

claims.claim: archiveArtifacts saves files on the controller for later retrieval.
claims.quote: and saves them to the Jenkins controller for later retrieval.

claims.claim: Archived artifacts are kept as long as the build's log is kept.
claims.quote: Normally, Jenkins keeps artifacts for a build as long as a build log itself is kept

claims.claim: archiveArtifacts fails the build when it archives nothing, unless allowEmptyArchive is set.
claims.quote: Normally, a build fails if archiving returns zero artifacts.
